title: Linux-LIRO boundary, UIPC/ADF/SDF and the command dispatcher
summary: How im.elf and Linux reach av-cam: shared-memory rings, UIPC framing, the [ADF]/[SDF]/[VDF]/[VEF] message families, and the 285-entry av_command_table.
questions: What is the exact shared-memory layout of the LIRO copy and the UIPC ring (header, slot size, producer/consumer indices, ownership)?
What are the argument and return conventions of an av_command_table handler, and what does the checker word gate?
How are ADF/SDF/VDF/VEF message families framed and routed, and which of them are synchronous?
Which command ids does im.elf send during boot (CheckerBootState, ObjMic, ObjPower), and what does av-cam do differently for a timeout?
deliverable: UIPC/command ABI specification with a byte-level ring contract and a table of the 285 command ids with handler signatures. Blocks M2.
